observations.observation: Height, organ size and most physiological capacities increase through childhood and adolescence toward a lifetime peak. These are developmental changes and are not age-associated deterioration.

effect.statement: Capacity rises toward a peak reached in early adulthood.

uncertainty.description: Timing of peak capacity varies by system and by individual, and differs between sexes for several measures.

observations.observation: The thymus begins involuting from early childhood, long before any other system shows age-associated decline, progressively reducing output of new naive T cells.

effect.statement: Thymic mass and naive T-cell output decline progressively from early life.

uncertainty.description: The functional consequence of involution is debated, since peripheral T-cell maintenance partly compensates. Onset in early childhood makes this hard to classify as straightforwardly age-associated.
known_conflicts: Thymic involution begins during development, so it does not fit neatly into either the developmental or the aging category.

observations.observation: Skeletal muscle mass declines with age in adult populations, with the decline more pronounced in the lower body than the upper body.

effect.statement: Muscle mass is lower on population average at older ages, with regional differences.

uncertainty.description: Cross-sectional data cannot separate aging from cohort effects, and physical activity is a large uncontrolled contributor. Individual variation is wide.

observations.observation: Muscle strength declines faster than muscle mass with age, so strength loss is not explained by mass loss alone. Current sarcopenia definitions therefore centre on strength rather than mass.

effect.statement: Strength declines disproportionately relative to mass.

uncertainty.description: Sarcopenia is a clinical condition with contested cut-points, and is distinct from normal age-associated muscle change. Where the boundary lies is a definitional choice, not a measurement.
known_conflicts: Diagnostic thresholds differ between working groups and populations.

observations.observation: The regenerative response of muscle satellite cells to injury is reduced in aged tissue, and is partly restored in animal models by exposure to a young systemic environment.

effect.reason: Human satellite-cell function is measured by heterogeneous assays that do not yield a comparable population figure.

uncertainty.description: The restoration evidence comes from parabiosis in mice, which has no human counterpart, and the responsible circulating factors are not fully identified.

observations.observation: Bone remodelling balance shifts with age such that resorption exceeds formation, reducing bone mineral density. The change is substantially faster in women in the years following menopause.

effect.statement: Bone mineral density declines, with a sex-specific acceleration after menopause.

uncertainty.description: This seed corpus uses a single mixed-sex population, which obscures a difference that is large and well documented. Sex-stratified content is needed before this record should be used for comparison.
known_conflicts: Mixed-sex population framing is inadequate for a change this strongly sex-dependent.

observations.observation: Large arteries stiffen progressively with age as elastin fragments and collagen content rises, increasing pulse wave velocity and systolic load on the heart.

effect.statement: Arterial stiffness increases across adult ages.

uncertainty.description: Separating normal arterial aging from subclinical atherosclerosis is difficult, and the cohorts are not globally representative.

observations.observation: The aging heart shows increased left ventricular wall thickness and slowed early diastolic filling, with maximal heart rate under exertion declining.

effect.statement: Filling dynamics and maximal rate change; resting output is often preserved.

uncertainty.description: Resting cardiac function is often well preserved, so these changes appear mainly as reduced reserve under stress rather than as resting impairment.

observations.observation: Cardiomyocytes are largely post-mitotic and accumulate damaged mitochondria with age, with reduced mitochondrial turnover capacity.

effect.reason: Mitochondrial damage burden in living human myocardium is not measurable by any routine method.

uncertainty.description: Most evidence is from animal tissue and post-mortem human samples. Whether mitochondrial change drives cardiac functional decline or accompanies it is unresolved.

observations.observation: The naive T-cell pool contracts with age while memory and terminally differentiated populations expand, narrowing the repertoire available to respond to novel antigens.

effect.statement: Repertoire composition shifts from naive toward memory and differentiated subsets.

uncertainty.description: Immune aging varies widely between individuals and is strongly affected by cytomegalovirus status, which is often unmeasured.
known_conflicts: Chronic viral exposure history is a major confounder that cohorts rarely control for.

observations.observation: Circulating inflammatory markers including interleukin-6 tend to be higher in older adults, and higher levels associate with frailty and adverse outcomes.

effect.statement: Inflammatory marker levels are higher on population average at older ages.

uncertainty.description: The causal direction is not established: inflammation may drive functional decline, result from it, or both. Marker levels also respond to infection, adiposity, medication and acute illness.
known_conflicts: Whether inflammaging is a cause or a consequence of frailty remains unresolved.

observations.observation: Haematopoietic stem cells show age-associated lineage bias toward myeloid output and reduced regenerative capacity per cell, even as their number does not decline.

effect.reason: Per-cell regenerative capacity is assayed by transplantation, which cannot be done in humans for this purpose.

uncertainty.description: The core functional evidence is from mouse transplantation assays. Human data are largely correlative and based on clonal composition rather than function.

observations.observation: Nephron number and measured filtration capacity decline with age, with substantial variation between individuals and considerable overlap with early kidney disease.

effect.statement: Filtration capacity is lower on population average at older ages.

uncertainty.description: Much of the structural data comes from living kidney donors, who are healthier than the general population. Distinguishing normal nephron loss from early disease is contested.
known_conflicts: Donor cohorts are health-selected, likely understating decline in the general population.

observations.observation: Brain volume decreases with age, with the change more pronounced in prefrontal and hippocampal regions than elsewhere, alongside changes in white matter integrity.

effect.statement: Regional brain volume is lower on population average at older ages.

uncertainty.description: Cognitive aging varies enormously between individuals, and separating normal aging from preclinical neurodegenerative disease remains unresolved in cross-sectional data.

observations.observation: Long-lived neurons depend heavily on proteostasis and autophagy to clear damaged proteins, and markers of impaired clearance increase with age in human brain tissue.

effect.reason: Autophagic flux cannot be measured directly in living human brain.

uncertainty.description: Post-mortem markers are static snapshots and cannot establish flux. Whether impaired clearance causes neuronal dysfunction or follows it is not resolved.

observations.observation: Human diploid fibroblasts in culture undergo a limited number of divisions before entering a stable growth-arrested state, an in-vitro limit associated with telomere shortening.

effect.reason: A replicative limit in culture does not correspond to a measurable population quantity in tissue.

uncertainty.description: This is an in-vitro phenomenon under culture conditions that differ substantially from tissue. It is often misread as demonstrating that cell division limits drive human aging, which it does not.
known_conflicts: The replicative limit is frequently over-extrapolated to whole-organism aging.

observations.observation: Markers used to estimate senescent-cell burden increase with age in multiple human tissues, though no single marker is reliable on its own.

effect.statement: Estimated senescent-cell burden is higher at older ages.

uncertainty.description: Senescence has no universal marker and phenotypes are heterogeneous, so burden estimates depend heavily on which markers are chosen.
known_conflicts: Different marker panels yield materially different burden estimates.

observations.observation: Telomere length measured in leukocytes is shorter on average at older ages, but the relationship is noisy and individual variation at any given age is large.

effect.statement: Average leukocyte telomere length is shorter at older ages.

uncertainty.description: Leukocyte measurements are a poor proxy for telomere state in other tissues, measurement methods differ substantially between studies, and within-age variation exceeds the between-age difference.
known_conflicts: Associations between telomere length and mortality are inconsistent across cohorts.

observations.observation: Methylation at selected CpG sites tracks chronological age closely enough to build accurate age predictors across many human tissues.

effect.statement: Predicted methylation age tracks chronological age across the lifespan.

uncertainty.description: A predictor trained on chronological age necessarily tracks chronological age; this establishes no mechanism. Epigenetic age is not a validated measure of any individual's functional state, and must not be read as one.
known_conflicts: Epigenetic age is widely misinterpreted as a measure of biological condition rather than a statistical predictor.

observations.observation: Gut microbiome composition shifts with age in adult cohorts, and in some cohorts increasing individual uniqueness associates with health measures and survival.

effect.statement: Composition shifts with age, with increasing between-individual divergence.

uncertainty.description: Diet, medication and residential care setting are severely confounded with age in these cohorts. No causal claim about the microbiome driving aging is supported in humans.
known_conflicts: Residential setting explains much of the composition difference in elderly cohorts.

observations.observation: Mitochondrial content and respiratory capacity change with age in a strongly tissue-dependent way, increasing in some tissues and decreasing in others.

effect.statement: Direction of change differs between tissues and cannot be summarised as a single trend.

uncertainty.description: Because the direction of change differs by tissue, any whole-body statement about mitochondrial decline is an oversimplification.
known_conflicts: The simple oxidative-damage account of mitochondrial aging is not supported.

observations.observation: Nutrient-sensing signalling through mTOR is implicated in aging across species, and its inhibition extends lifespan in several model organisms including mice treated late in life.

effect.reason: Pathway activity in human tissue across age is not systematically measured.

uncertainty.description: Lifespan extension is robust in mice but there is no human lifespan evidence, and mTOR inhibition carries immunosuppressive and metabolic costs that complicate translation.
known_conflicts: Benefits in mice differed by sex and come with meaningful adverse effects.

observations.observation: Lung elastic recoil decreases and alveolar surface area is reduced at older ages, lowering maximal ventilatory capacity while resting gas exchange is usually preserved.

effect.statement: Maximal ventilatory capacity declines while resting function is typically maintained.

uncertainty.description: Smoking history and environmental exposure are large confounders that are inconsistently controlled across the underlying literature.

observations.observation: Skin becomes thinner and less elastic with age and wound healing slows, with cumulative ultraviolet exposure contributing substantially to the observed change.

effect.statement: Elasticity and repair speed decline with age.

uncertainty.description: Photoaging from sun exposure is confounded with chronological aging in most skin data, and the two have different mechanisms and different reversibility.
known_conflicts: Photoaging and intrinsic skin aging are routinely conflated in the literature.

observations.observation: Lens proteins accumulate damage and cross-linking over decades, reducing accommodation and transparency, because lens crystallins are not replaced after development.

effect.statement: Accommodation and lens transparency decline with age.

uncertainty.description: The lens is an unusual case because its proteins are effectively never turned over, so it may not generalise to proteostasis in other tissues.
